tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Return the team's plan, its limits, current usage, the trial end date and the per-token MCP rate limit. Call it before deploy_site or add_custom_domain to check a plan limit instead of running into PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

tools.name: deploy_site
tools.description: Publish a static site or single-page app to a live HTTPS URL on the account's platform subdomain (e.g. {name}.subsite.site). A new name creates the site. An existing name REPLACES EVERY FILE (files not in this call are deleted) and needs confirm:"I-want-to-replace-all-files"; preview with dryRun:tru

tools.name: update_site
tools.description: Change files on an existing site. Default mode 'patch' writes only the listed files and keeps the rest; `delete: [paths]` removes files. mode:'replace' deletes every file not listed. Preview with dryRun:true. Use deploy_site instead to create a new site. A 100-250 KB text file fits in one call with

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the team's sites (name, URL, status, last deploy), most recently updated first, up to 100. Use list_sites to find a site name; use get_site for one site's files, source status and history.

tools.name: get_site
tools.description: Return one site's details: live URL, status, plan, served file paths, whether editable source is stored (and its build settings), custom domains, bandwidth and the last 10 deploys. Use get_site to inspect a site before editing it; use list_sites to find site names, and get_app_status for container s

tools.name: delete_site
tools.description: Soft-delete a site (confirm:true required). It stops serving at once and is purged after the plan's restore window (purgesAt in the result); until then the user can restore it in the VibeDeploy dashboard. Use delete_site to remove the whole site; use remove_app instead to stop only its container ser

tools.name: get_site_analytics
tools.description: Return a privacy-safe traffic summary for a site over the last `period` days (default 7): total page views, distinct-visitor count, top pages, daily counts, device/browser breakdowns, and Web Vitals averages. Never exposes raw visitor IPs or user-agents.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Return one file the site serves now, as text (utf8) or base64 for binary files, e.g. to edit it and send it back with update_site mode:'patch'. Use read_file for the served files; use read_source_file instead for the editable source tree (get_site.sourceStored). Max 5242880 bytes; get_site.filePaths

tools.name: read_files
tools.description: Read up to 50 served files in one call, with the same per-file rules as read_file and 8388608 bytes in total; paths past the budget fail with BATCH_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, so request them again in another call. Use read_source_files instead for the editable source tree.

tools.name: list_file_hashes
tools.description: Return SHA-256 and size of every served file. Before a redeploy, hash your local files, compare, and upload only the changed ones with update_site mode:'patch' or begin_deploy plus add_files.

tools.name: list_source_files
tools.description: List path, SHA-256 and size of every file in the site's editable source tree (the stored pre-build code, not the served files). Read-only. A site without a source tree returns SOURCE_NOT_STORED: write the source with write_source_files, or copy plain static served files with promote_dist_to_source.

tools.name: promote_dist_to_source
tools.description: Create the editable source tree of a site that has none by copying the files it serves, so later changes can use write_source_files, apply_edits(target:'source') and build_and_deploy. The served files do not change, and a site that already has source is left as is. Use mode 'force' only after tellin

tools.name: read_source_file
tools.description: Return one file from the site's editable source tree (the stored pre-build code), so any chat can edit the site without the original local files. list_source_files shows the paths. Use read_source_file for source; use read_file instead for the files the site serves.

tools.name: read_source_files
tools.description: Read up to 50 files from the editable source tree in one call (8388608 bytes in total). Each path succeeds or fails on its own; paths past the budget fail with BATCH_BUDGET_EXCEEDED. Use read_source_files for source; use read_files instead for the files the site serves.

tools.name: write_source_files
tools.description: Write or overwrite files in the site's editable source tree (the first write creates it). The served files do not change until build_and_deploy runs. Use list_source_files first to see what exists. A legacy site without source storage returns SOURCE_STORAGE_NOT_ENABLED; the user can ask VibeDeploy s

tools.name: delete_source_file
tools.description: Remove one file from the site's editable source tree. The served files do not change until build_and_deploy runs.

tools.name: build_and_deploy
tools.description: Build the site's stored editable source in an isolated one-shot build pod and atomically publish the output as the live site, replacing the served files (a restore point is normally taken first). Use build_and_deploy after changing stored source (write_source_files, apply_edits with target 'source')

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Search every file of a site for a literal string or a regular expression: the served files by default, or the editable source tree with target 'source'. Use it before reading files in bulk, to find the ones that matter.

tools.name: deploy_from_url
tools.description: Fetch a public tar(.gz) archive over HTTPS and deploy its files to an existing site in one call (begin_deploy, upload and commit_deploy combined). Use deploy_from_url when the files are already published at a public URL, such as a repository archive that holds only the built site (no dotfiles), or w

tools.name: rehost_images
tools.description: Download the external images a site references (e.g. from the old site it was rebuilt from), store them on this VibeDeploy site under assets/img/, and rewrite the HTML references to local paths so the site no longer depends on the original. Call this once AFTER deploying a site rebuilt with th

tools.name: update_file_content
tools.description: Apply literal find/replace edits to one file in one call, for small changes where uploading the whole file is wasteful. Each edit states how many matches it expects; any mismatch aborts the call with no writes. Served-file (dist) edits go live at once; source edits ship with build_and_deploy. Use ap

tools.name: apply_edits
tools.description: Apply literal find/replace edits to several files in one call, in the served files (target 'dist', live at once) or the editable source (target 'source', shipped by build_and_deploy). Same edit rules as update_file_content. All or nothing: if any edit's match count differs from its expected count, n

tools.name: get_forms_config
tools.description: Read the form-to-email relay config of a site, plus the resolved delivery mode, the active From address, and (for a custom sender domain) the DNS records to publish and their verification status. The submission format for the site's form is described under set_forms_config.

tools.name: set_forms_config
tools.description: Configure the built-in form-to-email relay, fully self-service. Supports a custom From (via a verified sender domain or your own SMTP relay), an explicit Reply-To, and full email branding (subject template, field labels/order, logo, accent color, or a custom HTML body). Requires team role owner or a

tools.name: verify_forms_sender_domain
tools.description: Check the DNS records for a site's custom sender domain (DKIM TXT + SPF include). Once the DKIM record is observed, the sender domain is marked verified and the relay sends from the custom From (DKIM-signed). Until then it falls back to the platform address. DNS can take a few minutes to propagate;

tools.name: add_custom_domain
tools.description: Start attaching a user-owned domain to an existing site: returns the DNS records the user adds at their DNS provider (a routing record that sends visitors here, plus a TXT that proves ownership). Idempotent: the same siteName and domain return the existing record. Once the records are published (usu

tools.name: verify_custom_domain
tools.description: Check the records from add_custom_domain (the ownership TXT and the routing record) and, when both are right, start serving the site on that domain; the HTTPS certificate follows automatically, usually within a minute or two. If it fails, the result names each record to add, change or remove; DNS ch

tools.name: remove_custom_domain
tools.description: Detach a custom domain from a site. The site itself is unaffected and keeps serving on its platform subdomain (e.g. {name}.subsite.site).

tools.name: list_custom_domains
tools.description: Return all custom domains attached to a site, both those added with add_custom_domain (source 'mcp', with a recordId for verify_custom_domain or remove_custom_domain) and those linked in the VibeDeploy dashboard (source 'dashboard', verified or removed on the dashboard Web Addresses page at manageUr

tools.name: list_dns_records
tools.description: Read the DNS records VibeDeploy tracks for a site (host, type, value), oldest first, including custom-domain verification records. Read-only: it never creates, changes or deletes a DNS record.

tools.name: check_domain_availability
tools.description: Check whether a domain can be registered and get an indicative price (VAT included where it applies). Read-only: it never buys, registers or reserves a domain. alternatives:true also checks the same name on be, com, net, eu, nl, io, dev and app. Not tied to a site. The result states whether the user

tools.name: begin_deploy
tools.description: Open a staging session for a deploy that is too large for one call: stage files with add_files (repeatable), add_file_chunk, or one tar(.gz) POST to the returned uploadUrl, then publish with commit_deploy. Use begin_deploy only when the files do not fit in one deploy_site or update_site call. Up to

tools.name: add_files
tools.description: Add files to an open begin_deploy session; call it as often as needed, then commit_deploy publishes them together. Paths, extensions and encodings are checked on every call. A 100-250 KB text file usually fits in one call with encoding:'gzip+base64' (gzip locally, then base64); prefer that over add_

tools.name: add_file_chunk
tools.description: Send one file in several calls when it is too big for a single tool call. Last resort: first try add_files with encoding:'gzip+base64' (about 250 KB of text in one call), begin_deploy's uploadUrl (one 100 MB tar POST) or deploy_from_url (public archive URL). When chunking, gzip+base64 each chunk too

tools.name: commit_deploy
tools.description: Publish a begin_deploy session's staged files to the live site in one atomic step, after a secret and malware scan of the complete set (on failure the session stays open to retry or abort). Replace mode on a site that has files needs confirm:"I-want-to-replace-all-files". After a timeout or dropped

tools.name: abort_deploy
tools.description: Discard a begin_deploy session and its staged files; the live site is untouched. Cleanup is best effort and retried later if it fails.

tools.name: list_deploys
tools.description: List the team's begin_deploy staging sessions, by default the active ones (open and committing), up to 50. Useful after a crash or restart to commit or abort leftovers.

tools.name: list_history
tools.description: Return the site's last 50 deploy and snapshot entries, newest first: how each was triggered, label, snapshot name, file count and secrets detected. Each entry's snapshot holds the content from BEFORE that entry. Restoring is done by the user in the VibeDeploy dashboard within the plan's restore wind

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: List the snapshots of a site's served files (point-in-time restore points). NO_VOLUME means the site was never deployed. Restoring a snapshot is done by the user in the VibeDeploy dashboard within the plan's restore window.

tools.name: create_snapshot
tools.description: Take a point-in-time snapshot of a site's served files, a restore point the user can restore in the VibeDeploy dashboard within the plan's restore window. Served content does not change, but retention cleanup may remove older snapshots. Container data is not included. Requires an owner or admin team

tools.description: Run container services next to a site, from any public image: the user's own server (running code from the site's source tree), a database such as Postgres or MySQL, Redis, or workers, each in a gVisor sandbox. The call applies the whole config: services missing from it are stopped (their volumes ar

tools.name: get_app_status
tools.description: Show the site's container services: per-service status (ready, restarts, waiting or crash reasons, volumes), the stored config, the names of the site secrets that are set (never values) with the dashboard link where the user adds them, the CPU / memory ceilings of this site (resourceCeilings), and o

tools.name: remove_app
tools.description: Stop every container service of the site; the site serves its static files again. Volumes (database data) are kept unless deleteData is true, which deletes them for good. Use remove_app to stop only the containers; use delete_site to remove the whole site.

findings.detail: Tool "read_file" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "deploy_site" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Publish a static site or single-page app to a live HTTPS URL on the account's platform subdomain (e.g. {name}.vibedeploy.be). A new name creates the site. An existing name REPLACES EVERY FILE (files not in this call are deleted) and needs confirm:"I-want-to-replace-all-files"; preview with dryRun:tr" → after: "Publish a static site or single-page app to a live HTTPS URL on the account's platform subdomain (e.g. {name}.subsite.site). findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
